Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the GlobalTech Solutions Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Emily Carter, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to GlobalTech Solutions’ Q3 2024 earnings call. With me today are Robert Thompson, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; David Lee, COO; and Maria Rodriguez, CTO.
Earlier today, we published our press release and earnings slides, which are available on our IR website. Please note that this call may contain forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to Robert.

Robert Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Emily, and welcome, everyone.

We had a solid quarter with performance driven by several key initiatives. First, I’d like to discuss our customer LTA and supply agreement update, including underutilization charges. During Q3, we successfully added five new LTAs to our portfolio, representing a crucial component of our strategic growth plan, ensuring predictable revenue streams and fostering deeper customer relationships. These five LTAs added a total of roughly $1.4 billion in contracted revenue over their respective terms, with an incremental $200 million recognized in revenue during Q3 via prepayments and access fees related to these new LTAs. Specifically, there was a 7-year agreement with GreenTech Solutions, a rapidly expanding renewable energy provider based in the US Northeast, which focuses on providing them with our advanced energy storage solutions. The total contract value is estimated at $450 million, with a prepayment of $75 million significantly boosting our Q3 revenue in the Energy Solutions segment. There was also a 5-year supply agreement with EuroAutomation AG, a leading industrial automation company in Germany. This LTA secures our position as their primary supplier of specialized components for their robotics manufacturing, with a total contract value of $300 million. We received an access fee of $40 million at the start of the contract, which was recognized as revenue in Q3. Additionally, we have a 10-year agreement with AsiaTelCom, a major telecommunications provider in Southeast Asia, involving the supply of advanced network infrastructure equipment, valued at $400 million, including a $60 million prepayment, recognized in Q3 revenue. A 3-year agreement with National Defense Systems, a leading U.S. defense contractor, secures our position as their prime supplier of specialized components for their advanced weaponry systems. The total contract value stands at $150 million, with an access fee of $15 million recognized in Q3. Finally, a 3-year agreement with Global Oil, a leading oil and gas company in the Middle East, has a total contract value of $100 million, with an access fee of $10 million recognized in Q3. Overall, the revenue contribution from our LTA portfolio was a significant driver in our Q3 results, contributing to a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion. While the overall LTA portfolio performed well, we did experience an underutilization event with one particular customer, MegaCorp Industries, a diversified manufacturing conglomerate. After extensive negotiations, we reached a settlement with MegaCorp Industries for an underutilization fee of $8 million.

We also made meaningful progress with our sales guidance and segment forecast for fiscal year 2023. Our fiscal year 2023 sales forecast reflects a bifurcated market environment. While we anticipate continued headwinds in the Communications, Infrastructure, and Data Center (CID) segment and ongoing softness in the PC and Notebook market, we project a gradual recovery beginning in the second half of the year, driven by strategic initiatives and a stabilization of macroeconomic conditions. Overall, we are guiding towards a conservative 3-5% decline in total revenue for FY2023. We expect revenue within the CID segment to decline throughout the first half of 2023, primarily due to inventory corrections, deferral of capital expenditures, and increased competition. We project a 12-15% decline in CID revenue in the first half of 2023, compared to the same period last year, translating to roughly $1.8 billion in revenue for H1 2023, down from $2.1 billion in H1 2022. We anticipate a gradual recovery in the second half of 2023, fueled by 5G infrastructure buildout, data center expansion, and strategic partnerships. We project a total decline of 6-8% for the CID segment for the full year 2023, assuming a stronger second half, with a projected flat to slightly positive growth rate in Q4 2023 compared to Q4 2022. The PC and Notebook market continues to experience a significant slowdown following the surge in demand during the pandemic, and we expect this segment to continue to decline as a percentage of our overall revenue in 2023. Specifically, we are forecasting a 20-25% decrease in PC and Notebook revenue for the full year 2023, translating to approximately $500-$550 million in revenue, down from $700 million in 2022. On the other hand, we are seeing continued strength in other end markets, particularly in Automotive and Industrial, and we project growth of 8-10% in these other end markets for the full year 2023, driven by the electrification of vehicles and increased adoption of automation technologies.

On a broader level, our CapEx guidance for the full year supported our positioning. As previously communicated, our full-year 2023 CapEx guidance remains unchanged at approximately $2.25 billion. This figure represents a 7% increase compared to the $2.1 billion spent in 2022, reflecting our commitment to strategic investments in infrastructure upgrades, technology advancements, and expanding our operational footprint in key growth markets. The $2.25 billion CapEx is allocated across three primary categories: Infrastructure Upgrades (45%, approximately $1.01 billion), Technology Advancements (35%, approximately $788 million), and Strategic Expansion (20%, approximately $450 million). Within infrastructure upgrades, roughly $350 million is dedicated to our North American facilities, $280 million is earmarked for our European operations, and $380 million is planned for upgrading facilities in Asia. For technology advancements, we have AI-Powered Predictive Maintenance ($250 million), Cloud Migration and Data Analytics ($300 million), and R&D for Next-Generation Products ($238 million). For strategic expansion, there's construction of a new manufacturing facility in Southeast Asia ($250 million), expansion of our distribution network in South America ($150 million), and a possible acquisition of key AI technology ($50 million). Q3 2023 CapEx spending was approximately $575 million, slightly ahead of our internal projections of $550 million, driven by the accelerated implementation of our AI-powered predictive maintenance program.

I’ll now hand it over to Sarah to walk you through the financials.

Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Robert, and hello, everyone.

This quarter’s financial results were underpinned by operational rigor and discipline. Let’s walk through the key metrics.

To start, our wafer sales and the breakdown to wafer quantity and ASP for this quarter helped drive improvements in our gross margins. We shipped approximately 511,300 equivalent 300mm wafers this quarter. This represents an 18% decrease compared to the 623,500 wafers shipped in Q3 2023. This decrease is not indicative of a broad weakening in demand, but rather a reflection of several key factors. We experienced a significant pullback in orders from our PC and consumer electronics customers. Also, ongoing geopolitical tensions and trade restrictions, particularly those impacting our ability to serve certain Chinese customers with advanced process nodes, had a noticeable effect. We are strategically shifting our production capacity towards higher-margin products, specifically those utilizing our advanced 7nm and 5nm process technologies. As part of our ongoing efforts to diversify our supply chain to mitigate future disruptions, we temporarily reduced orders from specific suppliers, which impacted our ability to fulfill certain lower-margin orders immediately. Despite the decrease in wafer volume, our Average Selling Price (ASP) increased by approximately 12% year-over-year. This increase is a testament to our commitment to innovation and our ability to capture value in the market. We saw strong demand for our 7nm and 5nm process technologies, particularly in the mobile, HPC (High-Performance Computing), and automotive sectors. We have successfully implemented value-based pricing strategies, reflecting the superior performance and reliability of our wafers. Favorable currency fluctuations, particularly the weakening of the Euro against the US dollar, contributed approximately 1% to the ASP increase. We are seeing strong growth in demand for our specialty process technologies, such as those used in power management ICs, RF (Radio Frequency) devices, and image sensors. Revenue from North America remained relatively stable, with a slight decrease of 2% year-over-year. Asia Pacific (Excluding China) saw strong growth, with revenue increasing by 15% year-over-year. Revenue from China decreased by approximately 25% year-over-year, primarily due to trade restrictions and geopolitical tensions. Revenue from Europe increased by 8% year-over-year, driven by strong demand for our specialty process technologies in the automotive and industrial sectors. We anticipate Q4 2024 wafer shipments to be roughly in line with Q3 2024 but expect a modest increase in ASP driven by increased adoption of our 5nm process. This results in an expected revenue decrease of roughly 16% year-over-year to $3.2 billion.

Additionally, our net margin and Diluted EPS results showed strong improvement. Our Q1 2024 adjusted net income reached approximately $290 million, representing a substantial increase of approximately $58 million compared to the first quarter of last year. This translates to adjusted diluted earnings of $0.52 per share for the quarter, exceeding both our internal projections and consensus estimates. Our Q1 2024 adjusted net margin reached 14.5%, a notable increase from the 12.8% recorded in Q1 2023. We experienced robust revenue growth across several key segments. Overall, Q1 revenue grew by 12% year-over-year, reaching $2.0 billion. Our cloud-based subscription service, "Project Nimbus," saw a 35% increase in revenue, contributing significantly to a more favorable revenue mix. Our ongoing operational efficiency initiatives, particularly those focused on supply chain optimization and automation within our manufacturing facilities, have yielded substantial cost savings. We implemented a new AI-powered predictive maintenance system across our key manufacturing sites, resulting in a 15% reduction in unplanned downtime and a 7% decrease in maintenance costs. While we continue to invest strategically in growth initiatives, we have maintained a disciplined approach to SG&A expense management, and we implemented a zero-based budgeting approach for discretionary spending, resulting in a 3% reduction in SG&A expenses as a percentage of revenue compared to Q1 2023. Our Asia-Pacific (APAC) region demonstrated exceptional performance, with a 20% increase in revenue and a corresponding improvement in net margin. In Q1, we repurchased approximately 1.5 million shares of our common stock at an average price of $45 per share, further enhancing EPS. Foreign exchange fluctuations had a minor negative impact on our EPS, reducing our reported earnings by approximately $0.01 per share. The development and successful implementation of our new CRM system played a crucial role in driving sales efficiency and improving customer retention, and the new system also led to a 12% decrease in our churn rate, which also had a positive impact on EPS.

Lastly, our P&L (revenue and gross margin) guidance for next quarter increased our profitability. We anticipate GlobalTech Footwear (GF) revenue to land between $1.81 billion and $1.85 billion for Q3, pointing to a projected growth rate of approximately 8-10% compared to the $1.68 billion recorded in Q3 of the previous fiscal year. We anticipate North America to contribute significantly to the overall revenue, projecting around $750-$770 million for the quarter. European markets are expected to generate between $450-$470 million, and the Asia-Pacific region is projected to contribute $510-$530 million. The revenue breakdown by product category is expected to be as follows: Athleisure Footwear: $700-$720 million, Performance Footwear: $550-$570 million, Outdoor Footwear: $300-$320 million, and Other Footwear: $260-$280 million. We project that approximately 45% of GF revenue will be generated through e-commerce channels. The projected adjusted gross profit of $498 million to $527 million translates to an adjusted gross margin of approximately 27.5% to 28.5%. We have implemented strategic price increases on select product lines to offset rising input costs. We have made significant progress in optimizing our supply chain, negotiating favorable contracts with key suppliers and diversifying our sourcing locations. The increasing proportion of revenue from higher-margin product categories is contributing to the overall improvement in gross margin. We are actively investing in automation and process improvements in our manufacturing facilities to reduce labor costs and improve efficiency. Finally, the adjusted operating profit guidance of $288 million to $327 million is a natural result of the revenue and gross margin expectations, as well as controlled operating expenses.

Now I’ll pass it to David to provide color on execution.

David Lee, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, Sarah.

From a delivery and operations standpoint, this was one of our more efficient quarters in recent memory.

A big part of that was our customer LTA and supply agreement update, including underutilization charges, which allowed us to enhance our relationships with key clients. To further mitigate the risk of underutilization in the future, we are implementing several key strategic initiatives. We are investing in advanced demand forecasting tools and processes, leveraging machine learning algorithms to improve the accuracy of our predictions. We are implementing a more proactive approach to customer engagement, including regular check-ins and collaborative planning sessions to identify potential risks and opportunities. We are exploring options to incorporate greater flexibility into our LTA terms, such as volume adjustments based on pre-defined market indicators. The Asia-Pacific region continues to be a strong growth area for our LTA portfolio, driven by the increasing demand for our products and services in the telecommunications and infrastructure sectors. Conversely, we are closely monitoring the economic conditions in Europe, particularly the impact of rising energy costs on industrial activity.

We also saw execution gains related to our wafer sales and the breakdown to wafer quantity and ASP for this quarter, including an improvement to our supply chain. We are committed to investing in the development and deployment of leading-edge process technologies, including our 3nm and 2nm nodes. We are expanding our portfolio of specialty process technologies to address the growing demand in the automotive, industrial, and medical sectors. We are committed to building strong relationships with our customers by providing them with innovative solutions and exceptional service. We are continuously working to optimize our manufacturing operations to improve efficiency and reduce costs, and this includes investing in automation and advanced process control technologies.

Lastly, we began pilots tied to our overall wafer ASP comments, and the by node or segment wafer ASP comments for this quarter, where early signs are promising. Our ongoing investments in advanced packaging technologies, such as 2.5D and 3D integration, are also contributing to ASP growth. We are also actively pursuing "Design-Technology Co-Optimization (DTCO)" initiatives with our key customers, allowing us to tailor our manufacturing processes to their specific designs and achieve better performance and yields, which translates to higher ASPs. We will continue to focus on securing long-term customer agreements, optimizing our product mix, and investing in advanced technologies to maintain our competitive edge and command premium pricing for our wafers.

Now I’ll turn it over to Maria to discuss our technology initiatives.

Maria Rodriguez, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, David.

On the technology side, our teams delivered important milestones across multiple streams.

First, we completed major feature work aligned with our sales guidance and segment forecast for fiscal year 2023, especially our technical initiatives. We are investing heavily in R&D to develop next-generation technologies for the CID market, including the development of advanced silicon photonics solutions for high-bandwidth optical interconnects, improving the efficiency and performance of GaN-based power amplifiers for 5G base stations, and developing AI-powered solutions for optimizing network performance and reducing energy consumption. We recently launched a new line of high-performance GPUs specifically designed for gaming laptops, which is expected to generate incremental revenue in the second half of the year.

We also rolled out enhancements supporting our utilization rate, and the utilization rate guidance for the next quarter and future outlook. We are scheduling planned downtime for essential upgrades and maintenance during Q1, focused on improving energy efficiency and implementing AI-driven resource allocation. We are also adjusting our utilization targets to ensure that we can consistently meet our stringent service level agreements (SLAs) and provide a superior customer experience. We are exploring the deployment of AI-powered predictive maintenance tools to minimize unplanned downtime and optimize resource allocation, and we are also actively pursuing renewable energy sources to reduce our operational costs and improve our environmental footprint.

One final point — we’ve made structural improvements to better enable our CapEx guidance for the full year or long term, the changes from the previous guidance, and the comments for this quarter. We are implementing AI-driven systems to predict equipment failures and optimize maintenance schedules across our global facilities. We are continuing our migration to a cloud-based infrastructure to improve scalability, security, and data accessibility. We are investing in research and development to develop innovative products and solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers, including a focus on sustainable materials and eco-friendly manufacturing processes.

Let’s now open the floor for Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Thanks. You mentioned gains in the CapEx guidance. What gives you confidence that these are sustainable?

Robert Thompson:
We're confident that our CapEx investments are sustainable because they are directly tied to our strategic growth priorities and long-term market trends. The investments in infrastructure upgrades are essential for maintaining our operational efficiency and meeting the growing demand for our products. The technology advancements are focused on driving innovation and creating new revenue streams. And the strategic expansion initiatives are designed to capitalize on high-growth markets and diversify our geographic footprint. We also have a disciplined approach to capital allocation and a strong track record of delivering returns on our investments.

Analyst 2:
On wafer sales, is this inventory correction in the PC sector a short-term blip or a sign of more structural challenges?

Sarah Chen:
While we expect the inventory correction to persist into the next quarter, we believe it is primarily a short-term phenomenon. The underlying demand for computing devices remains strong, and we anticipate a rebound in the PC market in H1 2025 as inventory levels normalize and new product cycles begin. We are also diversifying our revenue streams by focusing on higher-growth sectors such as automotive and industrial, which will help to mitigate the impact of any potential long-term challenges in the PC market.

Analyst 3:
Can you elaborate on early traction with the overall wafer ASP comments?

David Lee:
We are seeing strong early traction with our overall ASP growth. This is driven by increased demand for our advanced process nodes, successful execution of our value-based pricing strategies, and favorable currency fluctuations. We are also actively pursuing Design-Technology Co-Optimization (DTCO) initiatives with our key customers, allowing us to tailor our manufacturing processes to their specific designs and achieve better performance and yields, which translates to higher ASPs.

Analyst 4:
How are you thinking about long-term opportunity in utilization rate, and the utilization rate guidance for the next quarter and future outlook?

Maria Rodriguez:
We see significant long-term opportunity to improve our utilization rates through a combination of strategic capacity management, technological innovation, and proactive customer engagement. We are exploring the deployment of AI-powered predictive maintenance tools to minimize unplanned downtime and optimize resource allocation. We are also actively pursuing renewable energy sources to reduce our operational costs and improve our environmental footprint.

Closing

Robert Thompson:
Thanks again to everyone for joining us. We’re energized by the results this quarter and remain focused on disciplined execution and strategic expansion. Looking forward to sharing continued progress next time.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.
